## ✨ Highlights

- 📈 **Auto-scaling**: a node the Controller created on libvirt or Proxmox VE grows while it runs - vCPUs and memory plugged in, no restart, no connection lost - and comes back to its size once the load is gone. It reads HAProxy's idle time, the CPUs, the memory and OOM kills against thresholds you set, and journals every step. Start it in **observe** mode: it writes what it would do, without resizing anything.
- 🔁 **An update says what it installs, and a node says what its other slot holds**: the Controller's Update page names the release it installs - in red, and only with its version typed, when it is older than the node's -, the node says the release of the bundle before writing it, and `janusctl version` and the node page show the release in the slot an update writes over and a rollback boots.
- 🗂️ **The event log survives reboots and updates**: a node keeps its last thousand events, so what happened before an update - or before a revert - is still there after it.

## 📈 Auto-scaling

- **A policy per machine** - **Edit** on its card in the Controller's **Hypervisors** tab, `PATCH /api/machines/{id}`, or Terraform:
  - its mode: **observe**, **on**, or **paused**;
  - how far it grows (`max_vcpus`, `max_memory_mib`);
  - its thresholds, each one with a default.

  The machine's own size is where it starts and comes back to. Setting a policy, changing its maxima or removing it restarts the machine once, with room to grow. The mode and the thresholds change without a restart.
- **When it steps** (the defaults - HAProxy's documentation gives no number, these are Janus's starting points, all changeable):
  - **a vCPU more** when HAProxy is idle less than 30 % of the time, or the CPUs are more than 75 % busy, over 5 minutes;
  - **more memory** when less than 20 % is available for 2 minutes - at once after an OOM kill;
  - **back towards its size** once the load stayed low for 30 minutes, one step at a time.

  How it judges:
  - memory goes first on the way up (HAProxy reloads for a vCPU), vCPUs first on the way back;
  - every measurement is judged at the size the step would give;
  - the up and down thresholds can't overlap, so a machine never shrinks back as soon as it grew.
- **Observing** changes nothing. Each step it would take is journaled with the measurement that called for it, and simulated: the journal shows how far the machine would have grown, and when it would have come back.
- **Resizing** (**on**):
  - memory is only added while the host keeps a twentieth of its own free;
  - each step waits until the node shows it, and journals what the machine really has;
  - a paused machine goes back to its size.
- **The kernel parameters follow** (`sysctl`):
  - the node's own suggestions - `tcp_mem`, `file-max` and `nf_conntrack_max` sized for the memory it has now, and the rest of **System › Sysctl**'s - are applied on trial, then confirmed once the node and HAProxy still answer;
  - never a parameter someone else set, and put back once the machine is at its size.
- **On the machine's card**: its mode, what auto-scaling says now, its warnings, and the **Journal**. A threshold no step can fix is said, not acted on: HAProxy near its `maxconn`, threads fixed by `nbthread`.
- **libvirt**: hot-plugged vCPUs and a virtio-mem device, changed in 128 MiB steps.
- **Proxmox VE 9.2**: hot-plugged vCPUs, and memory modules of 512 MiB above a static 1024 MiB - a scalable machine's memory is 1024, 1536, 2048 MiB and so on.

## 🖥️ Nodes

- **vCPUs and memory plugged in while a node runs**:
  - the kernel takes hot-plugged memory (virtio-mem, ACPI memory modules) and puts it where it can be taken back;
  - init brings hot-plugged vCPUs online, and HAProxy reloads to run a thread per CPU - unless its configuration fixes `nbthread` or `cpu-map`;
  - the event log says what changed: `system.cpus_changed`, `system.memory_changed`.
- **OOM kills**: each one is an event (`kernel.oom_kill`, naming the process the kernel killed), and the count since boot is in the `Memory` call and `janusctl system info`.
- **`net.ipv4.tcp_mem`** joins the kernel parameters you can change on trial: the memory TCP may take for all its sockets, which the kernel sizes once, at boot. Memory plugged in later doesn't change it, nor `file-max` or `nf_conntrack_max`: a new suggestion (`follow_memory`) gives the boot's value in proportion to the memory now.

## 🔁 Updates

- **The node page's Update names what it installs**: the latest release, a pre-release or a prepared image is named above the form, in the confirmation's title and on its button. One older than the release the node runs is flagged in red, and installing it takes its version typed - going back stays possible, never by accident. **Use this update** is offered only for a newer release.
- **The node says what it installs**, before writing anything: `rootfs.squashfs: Janus v2026.10.14 (schematic a055fbb6)`, with `older than the … this node runs` when it is, then `rebooting into slot B (Janus v…)`. On the Controller's page, the toast says it; `janusctl lifecycle upgrade` prints it.
- **The other slot**: `janusctl version` has `Other slot: A - v2026.10.13-4, schematic …, HAProxy …, kernel …`, and the node page's Update › This node an **Other slot** line - the release an update writes over, and the one a rollback boots; the installation's confirmation names what it replaces. Read off the slot itself: an image from before v2026.10.06-3 says it doesn't know.

## 🗂️ Event log

- **Kept on the node** (STATE): its last thousand events come through janusd's restarts, the node's reboots and its updates - a revert included -, IDs going on. Written to disk within 5 seconds, and before every reboot. A Reset wipes it, with the rest of STATE.
- **Each start of janusd** is the first event of its run, with the release and the slot it started on: the node page's **Events** draws it as a line of its own, and dates the events of another day - so does `janusctl tui`.
- `lifecycle.upgrade` says the release it installed and the one it replaced.

## 🧱 Terraform

- **`janus_node.autoscaling`**:
  - the block holds the mode, the maxima, `sysctl` and every threshold (optional - unset, the Controller's default);
  - `vcpus` and `memory_mib` stay the size the node starts with and comes back to. What auto-scaling gives it isn't drift: it reads back as `current_vcpus` and `current_memory_mib`.

## 🐛 Fixes

- **`option socket-stats`**: a frontend's listeners (one row per bind in HAProxy's statistics) were listed as a backend with servers by `janusctl haproxy backends` and the node page's Backends, and as servers in `janusctl tui` - while a frontend without the option didn't show, as if it were missing. Rows are now told apart by their type: listeners and frontends never appear as backends or servers ([#64](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/64)).

## 📦 Components

- **BIRD** (the BGP extension): 2.19.3 → 2.20.0. No known vulnerability fixed.
- **The kernel** (both tracks): memory hot-plug, virtio-mem and ACPI memory hot-plug built in, for auto-scaling.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update. Auto-scaling needs a node on this release: its kernel takes plugged-in memory. The event log is kept from this release on: the update to it is the last one that starts with an empty log. The other slot is shown once the node runs this release.
- **The Controller**: update it from its update card. Existing machines don't change: auto-scaling is off until a machine gets a policy, and setting one restarts that machine once. Start with **observe** on real traffic, then turn it **on**.
- **janusctl**: `apt update && apt install janusctl`, or the release's `.deb` - `version`'s other slot, OOM kills in `system info`, and the TUI without listeners among the servers.
- **The Terraform provider**: the release's archives - `janus_node.autoscaling`, `current_vcpus` and `current_memory_mib`.
